verdict.rationale: Elastic's docs describe a getting-started path to create a project, index data with your preferred language, and run searches in 10 minutes. There is also a one-liner Docker quickstart (`curl -fsSL https://elastic.co/start-local | sh`) and a free serverless trial, so the story's core is directly documented. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the quickstart actually completes in minutes, and step-level evidence of the explicit create-index and add-documents API calls (the evidence is summary claims only).

support.subject: As a developer, I can create an index, add documents, and run my first search within minutes of starting the quickstart

citations.quote: Create a project, then use your preferred language to index data and run semantic and hybrid searches in 10 minutes.
Quickly set up Elasticsearch and Kibana in Docker for local development or testing, using this one-liner in the command line.
All you need to do is create an index mapping to start ingesting, embedding, and querying data.
If you are a new user, sign up for a free 14-day trial to create a serverless project.
